questions.prompt: Complete both blanks: "If the students ___ (not read) the instructions carefully, they ___ (make) mistakes."

options.text: won't read ... make
doesn't read ... will make
don't read ... will makes
don't read ... will make

questions.explanation: "don't read ... will make": the students are they, so the negative in the if clause is don't + base verb, and the result takes will + base verb. "won't read ... make" swaps the tenses; "doesn't" is only for he, she, it; "will makes" adds an -s after will.

questions.prompt: Jenny's chain begins: "If I get lost, I'll check my map." Which next link is correct?

options.text: If I will check my map, I find the hotel.
If I check my map, I will find the hotel.
If I checked my map, I will find the hotel.
If I check my map I will find, the hotel.

questions.explanation: "If I check my map, I will find the hotel." — the result "I'll check my map" becomes the next condition, so it goes back to the simple present (check), and the new result takes will. Copying "will check" into the if clause is the chain mistake; "checked" is the past; the comma belongs after the if clause.

questions.prompt: Rewrite with the if clause first: "You won't be tired tomorrow if you go to bed early."

options.text: If you go to bed early, you won't be tired tomorrow.
If you will go to bed early, you aren't tired tomorrow.
If you go to bed early you won't be, tired tomorrow.
If you won't go to bed early, you will be tired tomorrow.

questions.explanation: "If you go to bed early, you won't be tired tomorrow." — the if clause moves to the front with a comma after it, and nothing else changes. The other versions move will into the if clause, put the comma inside the result, or change the meaning with won't in the condition.

questions.prompt: Four pupils wrote about a trip. Which sentence contains a grammatical error?

options.text: If Omar misses the bus, he will take a taxi.
If Nour doesn't find her ticket, she won't travel.
If Sana arrives early, she will get a good seat.
If Tarek don't hurry, he will miss the plane.

questions.explanation: "If Tarek don't hurry, he will miss the plane." is wrong: Tarek is he, so the negative is "doesn't hurry". The other three sentences are correct: simple present with -s for he or she (misses, doesn't find, arrives), and will / won't + base verb in the result.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has the correct tenses AND the correct punctuation?

options.text: If the plane is late we'll wait, at the airport.
If the plane is late, we'll wait at the airport.
We'll wait at the airport, if the plane is late.
If the plane will be late, we'll wait at the airport.

questions.explanation: "If the plane is late, we'll wait at the airport." — simple present in the if clause, we'll (we will) in the result, and a comma after the if clause because it comes first. The comma does not go inside the result, nor before a second if clause; "will be" does not belong in the if clause.

questions.prompt: Complete: "If my brother ___ (not finish) his homework tonight, he ___ (not go) to the match on Sunday."

options.text: don't finish ... won't go
doesn't finish ... won't goes
won't finish ... doesn't go
doesn't finish ... won't go

questions.explanation: "doesn't finish ... won't go": my brother is he, so the if clause takes doesn't + base verb, and the negative result takes won't + base verb. "don't" is not for he; "won't goes" adds an -s after won't; "won't finish ... doesn't go" swaps the two negatives.
